config.title: Controlled DatePicker

intro.title: Controlled DatePicker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a controlled DatePicker component in React with TypeScript. You will learn how to manage the selected date using React state, ensuring the component's value is controlled by your application. The core programming concept is controlled components, where form elements like date inputs are driven by React state and update via event handlers. You will use TypeScript interfaces to define the component's props, including the current date value and an onChange callback function. By the end, you'll have a reusable DatePicker that synchronizes user input with your app's state in a type-safe way.
intro.usecase: Controlled DatePickers are essential in any form or data-entry interface where user input must be validated and synchronized with application state. You'll see them in travel booking sites for selecting flight dates, in financial dashboards for filtering transaction reports by date range, and in project management tools for setting task deadlines. As a developer, implementing a controlled DatePicker ensures the selected date is always available in your React state, enabling immediate validation, formatting, and submission with the rest of your form data.

objectives: Initialize and manage a Date state variable using React's useState hook
Configure a DatePicker component with controlled value and onChange props
Bind the DatePicker's value to the React state variable
Implement a handler function to update state when the date selection changes
Render the DatePicker component with controlled behavior in a functional component
Manipulate the date state through user interactions with the DatePicker
Integrate the controlled DatePicker with other form elements in a React application

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DatePicker that returns an empty JSX fragment (<></>).
steps.hint: Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should return JSX.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the DatePicker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A DatePicker component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component is defined as a function that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component returns JSX (like an empty fragment).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it DatePicker and it returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize the selectedDate state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, initialize a state variable named selectedDate using useState. Set its initial value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<string>('');
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a state variable
const [username, setUsername] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a selectedDate state variable initialized to an empty string, ready to store the user's selected date.
successCriteria: selectedDate state variable is declared using useState
Initial value is set to an empty string
TypeScript type annotation is used for the string type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with the correct syntax and setting the initial value to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Remember to use useState with an empty string as the initial value.

steps.title: Define the handleDateChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your DatePicker component, create a function named handleDateChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> as a parameter and updates the selectedDate state with the event's current target value.
steps.hint: The function should call setSelectedDate with the value from event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleDateChange function that can be used as an onChange handler for a date input.
successCriteria: The handleDateChange function is defined, takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and calls setSelectedDate with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes the correct parameter type and updates the state using setSelectedDate with the input value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDateChange function is not defined correctly. Check that it takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and calls setSelectedDate with event.target.value.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: Return a div element from the DatePicker component to serve as the main container.
steps.hint: Replace the existing return statement with one that returns a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element as its main container.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a div element from the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element. Check your return statement syntax.

steps.title: Add a label for the DatePicker
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add a label element with the text 'Select a date:'.
steps.hint: Add a <label> tag with the text content 'Select a date:' as the first element inside the div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a label to a form element
<label>Enter your name:</label>
steps.expectedOutcome: A label element with the text 'Select a date:' appears as the first child inside the container div.
successCriteria: The label element with text 'Select a date:' is present inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an accessible label for the date input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a label element with the exact text 'Select a date:' inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label element is missing or incorrect. Add a label with the text 'Select a date:' inside the container div.

steps.title: Add the date input element
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, after the label, add an input element with its type attribute set to 'date'.
steps.hint: Use the HTML input element with type='date' to create a date picker UI.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now contains a date input element after the label.
successCriteria: An input element with type='date' is added inside the div after the label.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure its type attribute is set to 'date'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The date input element is missing or incorrect. Add an <input type="date" /> element after the label.

steps.title: Wire the input value to the state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, set the value attribute of the date input element to the selectedDate state variable.
steps.hint: In React, you bind an input's value to state using the value attribute. Use the state variable directly.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: binding an input value to state
<input type="text" value={inputValue} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The date input will become a controlled component, with its value bound to the selectedDate state.
successCriteria: The input element has a value attribute set to selectedDate
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the value attribute to the input element and set it to selectedDate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element should have a value attribute bound to the selectedDate state variable.

steps.title: Wire the onChange event to the handler
steps.instruction: Set the onChange attribute of the input element to the handleDateChange function.
steps.hint: Add the onChange prop to the existing input element and assign it the handleDateChange function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an event handler to an input
<input type="text" onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element now has an onChange attribute that calls handleDateChange when the date changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the onChange attribute is set to handleDateChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onChange event is not properly connected. Check the input element's attributes.
